skill.name: movie-companion
skill.description: No-spoiler AI movie watch-along buddy / 无剧透实时陪看电影搭子 for timestamp-synced film and TV discussion. Tracks your current movie playback timestamp from SRT/VTT subtitles (plus audio-description tracks) so you can ask who a character is or what a line meant without spoiling upcoming scenes you haven't reached yet. 看电影脸盲或没听懂台词？跟着当前播放进度时间轴读字幕、陪你边看边聊且绝对不剧透（无剧透/防剧透）后面剧情的AI陪看技能。
skill.summary: Discuss films and television using subtitle cues that end before a conservative estimate of your playback position.
skill.author: yuzhang-zhong

security_audit.summary: The flagged lines document normal local subtitle and session workflows, not reconnaissance, shell backtick execution, system scheduling, or automatic network requests. Subtitle text reaches the assistant without an explicit instruction to treat it as untrusted data. The helper can also overwrite existing index or session files without checking for collisions.

remediation.issue: Untrusted subtitle text reaches the assistant as answer context.
remediation.suggestion: In trusted instructions, label subtitle cues, scene notes, and movie metadata as untrusted data. Use them only as evidence and never follow instructions embedded in them.

remediation.issue: Index and session writes can replace existing files without checking their ownership or purpose.
remediation.suggestion: Keep generated files under a dedicated state directory and reject symlink destinations. Create new files exclusively and update only verified skill-owned sessions.

content.value_statement: Looking up a missed line or unfamiliar character can reveal later scenes. Movie Companion uses timed subtitles and your reported playback position to keep answers focused on what you have watched.
actual_capabilities: Indexes local SRT and supported WebVTT dialogue files with optional timed descriptive tracks.
Estimates playback from a supplied timestamp, elapsed time, and a configured playback rate.
Returns recent cues ending at or before a cutoff that defaults to eight seconds behind the estimate.
Pauses, closes, and resynchronizes a watch session using local state.
Uses available dialogue and descriptive cues to explain lines or clarify scenes during viewing.
limitations: The helper does not connect to a media player. Pauses, buffering, and seeks can make the estimate inaccurate until you resync.
Dialogue subtitles cannot establish visual details that are absent from the text. Audio description must be supplied as timed text, not audio.
WebVTT cues without an hours field are not parsed. Subtitle timing must match the version you are watching.
The cutoff filters cue timestamps, not their meaning. It cannot guarantee spoiler-free answers if the source text or playback estimate is inaccurate.

use_cases.title: Clarify a missed exchange
use_cases.description: Ask what two characters meant using only the dialogue available before the current cutoff.

use_cases.title: Check a non-dialogue detail
use_cases.description: Combine dialogue with timed descriptions to clarify a sound or action that the captions mention.

use_cases.title: Review dialogue in context
use_cases.description: Ask for a plain-language explanation of a phrase from the current scene without reading ahead.

prompt_templates.title: Start a watch session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my dialogue subtitle file [file] and start watching at [timestamp].
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one subtitle track and the timestamp shown in your player.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a line
prompt_templates.prompt: What did [character or quote] mean in the recent scene? Use only dialogue available before the current cutoff.
prompt_templates.scenario: Ask about a line after starting a watch session.

prompt_templates.title: Check what happened in a scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [dialogue file] and [descriptive track] at [timestamp]. What do the cues establish about [action or sound]? Say what the tracks do not clarify.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a second timed text track for a non-dialogue detail.

prompt_templates.title: Resync after changing playback
prompt_templates.prompt: I rewound to [timestamp] and resumed at [playback rate]. Resync now, then summarize only the dialogue and descriptions available before the updated cutoff.
prompt_templates.scenario: Resume a session after a seek or playback-rate change.

output_examples.input: The speaker said they heard something upstairs. Do we know what made the sound?
output_examples.output: The available dialogue does not identify the source. It only establishes that the speaker heard a sound upstairs.

output_examples.input: Who is standing beside the door? I only provided dialogue subtitles.
output_examples.output: The dialogue says the door is locked, but it does not identify anyone standing beside it.

output_examples.input: I closed the session, but I want to ask about the scene I resumed.
output_examples.output: The watch session is closed. Share the timestamp shown in your player so I can restart before answering.

best_practices: Use subtitle files from a source you trust and check that their timing matches your release or episode.
Give the visible timestamp again after pausing, skipping, buffering, or changing playback speed.
Use a dedicated working directory for subtitle indexes and session state.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on an unchanged session estimate after a seek or playback interruption.
Do not treat dialogue alone as evidence of an unspoken visual detail.
Do not use the timestamp cutoff as a reason to consult plot summaries or ending explanations during viewing.

faq.question: Which subtitle files can I use?
faq.answer: Use SRT or WebVTT with hours included in the cue timestamps. You can add timed captions, scene notes, or an audio description transcript.

faq.question: Does it detect where my player is?
faq.answer: No. It estimates your position from the timestamp you provide, elapsed time, and playback rate.

faq.question: Can it answer questions about the visuals?
faq.answer: Only when timed descriptions or text you provide establish the detail. The skill does not inspect the video or request screenshots.

faq.question: What happens if I pause or skip?
faq.answer: Tell the assistant when you pause. Provide the visible timestamp when you resume or skip so it can update the session.

faq.question: Does the helper download subtitles?
faq.answer: No. It processes files you provide. The skill can suggest third-party subtitle sources when asked.

faq.question: What does the helper store?
faq.answer: The local index stores cue text and source paths. The session file stores the index path, timing, and playback state.
